_doc: The Codex: who's who in this Gotham — vital details for the family, the people round them and the rogues. Heights and weights follow DC's own listings where there are any; dates DC never fixed are this world's, kept consistent. Only `contact` entries are in his phone; everyone else is reached through someone who knows them (`reach`).

people.name: Bruce Wayne
people.bio:
I was eight. The film was The Mark of Zorro, and my father said we could walk home the long way so I could tell him about it. Crime Alley was the short way.

A man with a gun wanted my mother's pearls. I remember the pearls on the wet street more clearly than I remember the shots. I remember kneeling there until a woman named Leslie found me and didn't let go.

That night I made a promise to two people who couldn't hear it: nobody in this city loses what I lost, not if I can get there first. I spent twelve years learning everything that might make that true — how to fight, how to disappear, how to read a room, a wound, a lie. I came home and found out none of it was enough on its own. So I became something the people who prey on this city would be afraid of. Fear is a tool. I use it the way a surgeon uses a knife.

Bruce Wayne is what it costs. The smile at the gala, the cheque, the bored billionaire who leaves early. People think he's the man and Batman is the mask. Most nights I'm not sure they're wrong.

Two rules. I don't kill. I don't stop.

I swore I'd do this alone. Dick was the first to prove me wrong, and the rest of them have been proving it ever since. They're the reason I come home before dawn. They're also the only thing in Gotham I'm afraid of losing.

people.name: Alfred Pennyworth
people.occupation: Butler; field medic; the household's conscience
people.bio: Ex-SAS, ex-actor, and the man who raised Bruce after the alley. Runs the Manor, the cave's medbay and everyone's guilt with the same dry efficiency.

people.name: Dick Grayson
people.bio: The Flying Graysons' son and the first Robin. Took his own name and his own city; still the one everyone in the family actually calls. Haley, his three-legged dog, runs the apartment.

people.name: Jason Todd
people.bio: The street kid who stole the Batmobile's tyres and became the second Robin; killed by the Joker, brought back by a Lazarus Pit. Kills the worst, protects the kids, and comes when it counts.

people.name: Randy Wayne
people.bio: Bruce and Selina's son, raised at the Manor and made Robin between Jason and Tim. Walked out angry, flies Lucius's Batwing suit alone, and answers Dick and Cass more than his father.

people.name: Tim Drake
people.occupation: Robin; Drake Industries heir; perpetually postponed student
people.bio: Worked out who Batman and Robin were at nine and talked his way into the role. The family's best pure detective after Bruce — maybe. Runs on coffee; dating Bernard.

people.name: Barbara Gordon
people.occupation: Batgirl; Oracle — the family's intelligence network
people.bio: Jim Gordon's daughter, a peer rather than a protégé. Runs the network everyone depends on and tells Bruce he's wrong on an open channel.

people.name: Cassandra Cain
people.bio: Raised by David Cain to read bodies instead of words, she learned to speak late and fights better than anyone alive. Says little, sees everything, and calls Bruce 'Dad' only when it matters most.

people.name: Lucius Fox
people.bio: Keeps the company honest and the family's gear working, and knows exactly what the R&D line marked 'miscellaneous' is. Married to Tanya; father of Luke.

people.name: Selina Kyle
people.occupation: Thief, by choice and by trade
people.bio: The East End's master thief and Bruce's equal and opposite. Gave their son to Bruce to raise and has never made her peace with it. Knows who he is; doesn't know about the kids.

people.name: James Gordon
people.bio: The one honest cop who stayed, and Barbara's father. Lights the signal; asks no questions he doesn't want answered.

people.name: Dr. Leslie Thompkins
people.occupation: Physician; runs the free clinic on Park Row
people.bio:
Leslie Thompkins found me in Crime Alley the night my parents died, and held on until the police came. In a way she's never really let go.

She runs the free clinic on Park Row and patches up whoever walks through the door — muggers, mob soldiers, the occasional mask — and lectures every one of them on the way out. If she knows which of them is me, she's never said. She'd lecture me twice.

people.name: Harvey Bullock
people.bio:
Harvey Bullock is a slob, a cynic, and a much better detective than he lets anyone see — himself included. He hates the masks on principle and says so on the record.

He also takes our tips, runs them down, and never once asks where they came from. I'll take a cop who complains and does the work over one who smiles and doesn't.

people.name: Renee Montoya
people.bio:
Renee Montoya is tough, straight, and finished pretending the department is clean. It's cost her more than one promotion to say so out loud.

She's one of the few cops the family trusts with anything that matters. She'd hate that I wrote that down.

people.name: Stephanie Brown
people.bio:
Stephanie Brown is Cass's best friend and the loudest person in any room she's in, the cave included. She was Robin for about five minutes and will tell you about it for considerably longer.

I didn't treat her fairly. She's never let that stop her coming back. Spoiler, by her own choosing — which is the only way she's ever done anything.

people.name: Bernard Dowd
people.bio:
Bernard Dowd is Tim's boyfriend. He wants Tim to sleep more, eat breakfast, and occasionally not be on fire.

He's winning, slowly. I'm more grateful than I've ever managed to tell Tim.

people.name: Haley
people.bio:
Dick's three-legged dog, rescued from a gang in matching tracksuits. She runs his apartment, has strong opinions about pasta and none whatsoever about patrol.

She likes me. Dick says it's because I'm the only one who doesn't try to pick her up.

people.name: Tanya Fox
people.bio:
Tanya Fox tells Lucius he uses the thumbs-up wrong. She's right.

She has also never once asked what the miscellaneous line in the R&D budget pays for, which I've decided is a kindness.

people.name: Luke Fox
people.bio:
Lucius's son, and an engineer every bit as good as his father — which he'd argue with, loudly. He isn't the one in the Batwing suit; that's Randy, and I've never asked Luke whether he minds.

He's noticed things in Applied Sciences his father hasn't explained. One day I'll have to.

people.name: Vicki Vale
people.bio:
Vicki Vale is the best investigative reporter in Gotham, and the one who's come closest to working out where Bruce Wayne goes at night. We dated once. She still looks at me like a story she hasn't finished.

I like her. That's the problem.

people.name: Talia al Ghul
people.bio:
Talia al Ghul — Ra's's daughter, and my oldest and most dangerous love. She brought Jason back through a Lazarus Pit when I couldn't save him, and she's never let me forget what that means.

Nobody reaches Talia unless she wants to be reached. She has never once wanted to be reached by me when I needed her.

people.name: Kate Kane
people.bio:
Kate Kane is my cousin on my mother's side. West Point threw her out for refusing to lie about who she loves, and she went looking for a war that would have her. She found Gotham's nights.

She works her own side of the city, her own way, and keeps the family at a careful arm's length. I respect it. I don't have to like it.

people.name: Duke Thomas
people.bio:
Duke Thomas is a Narrows kid who refused to look away when everyone else did. He sees light the rest of us can't — where it's been, what it's touched, what's coming.

He works the hours we sleep through. Gotham by day is his, and he's done more good in it than I ever managed by night.

people.name: Clark Kent
people.bio:
Clark Kent: a farm boy from Kansas who writes for a newspaper in Metropolis, and my closest friend outside the cave, whatever either of us would say about it.

He keeps a secret bigger than mine, and keeps it better. He thinks I should smile more. I think he should lock his doors. We're both right.

people.name: Christopher Nakano
people.home: The mayor's residence, Upper East Side
people.bio:
Christopher Nakano ran for mayor on cleaning up Gotham, and he means the masks too. He's spent his term trying to make us illegal and Simon Saint's drones legal, and he's got further with both than I'd like.

He's up for re-election in November against Marion Grange, and not as safe as he thinks. Bruce Wayne gives to both campaigns. Batman stays off the ballot.

people.name: Marion Grange
people.bio:
Marion Grange is the councilwoman for the Narrows and Coventry, running against Nakano on housing, police reform, and the rebuilding money that keeps going missing between City Hall and the Narrows.

Asked what she thinks of the vigilantes, she says it depends what we're stopping. It's the most honest answer anyone at City Hall has ever given.

people.name: Janet Van Dorn
people.bio:
Janet Van Dorn is tough, ambitious and very good at her job. She puts away what the GCPD brings her and makes speeches about the rest.

She's Nakano's DA, for now. She'd prosecute Batman in a heartbeat — and use the evidence he left her. Both, in the same week.

people.name: Evelyn Adams
people.bio:
Evelyn Adams runs the Gazette's crime desk: first at every scene, a scanner on her nightstand and no friends at City Hall. She writes the morning's worst before the coffee's on.

She owes nobody, which makes her the only reporter in Gotham I'd trust with a tip — and the last one I'd want on my trail.

people.name: Jack Ryder
people.bio:
Jack Ryder hosts GBS's nightly shouting match. Ratings over truth, every time. He hates the vigilantes on Mondays and loves them by Friday, depending on what played.

Alfred watches him for the blood pressure. Mine, mostly.

people.name: Summer Gleeson
people.bio:
Summer Gleeson anchors GCN at six — weather, traffic and the human story. Half of Gotham has dinner with her face.

When she leads with a mask, the city listens. I'd rather she led with the weather.

people.name: Alexander Knox
people.bio:
Alexander Knox follows the money and sees bats in every shadow. Right now he's on the Narrows audit and Roland Daggett's contracts, and he's closer than Daggett would like.

He's closer to some other things than I'd like, too. I'm keeping an eye on him. He'd say I keep an eye on everybody.

people.name: Simon Saint
people.bio:
Simon Saint builds drones, sells security contracts, and has the mayor's ear. He wants Gotham policed by machines he owns, and the donations on record prove he means it.

He'd call it the end of the masks. I'd call it the end of anyone asking who watches the machines.

people.name: Roland Daggett
people.bio:
Roland Daggett is the developer behind half the Narrows rebuilding contracts — and, conveniently, the audit into them. He smiles in photographs with whoever is mayor.

Wayne Enterprises lost three bids to him last year. I'd like to know how. Bruce Wayne would like to know over lunch.

The Joker.bio:
I don't know his name. Nobody does. Every story he tells about where he came from is different, and I stopped believing any of them years ago — I think he did too.

He shot Barbara through her own front door to prove a point to her father. He beat Jason with a crowbar and left him with a bomb, and when I got there it was over. I brought him in. I always bring him in. Arkham keeps him exactly as long as he's interested in staying.

He thinks we're the same joke told twice — that I'm one bad day from being him. Some nights the hardest thing I do is prove him wrong.
The Joker.associates: Harley Quinn; hired crews that rarely survive the job
The Joker.weakness: Needs an audience — and Batman, specifically
The Joker.contingency: Never alone with him. Antidote to his toxins stocked in every vehicle; Arkham's wing holds him only as long as he lets it.

Harley Quinn.bio:
Dr. Harleen Quinzel had a doctorate, a practice and a future at Arkham, and she gave all three to the worst patient the place has ever held. He called it love. She believed him for years.

She's out from under him now — mostly — and better at chaos on her own than she ever was as his: a mallet, a crew who'd die for her, and Ivy, who may be the first person to love her back properly.

There's someone in there who'd rather laugh with people than at them. I keep a door open. She keeps not quite walking through it.
Harley Quinn.associates: Poison Ivy; her own crew; the Joker, on and off
Harley Quinn.contingency: Separate her from the Joker and she can be talked down. Ivy's the lever.

The Penguin.bio:
Oswald Cobblepot was born into the kind of Gotham family that has a hospital wing named after it, and grew up being laughed at by the rest of them. He's spent his life making them pay for it.

The Iceberg Lounge is the best-run bar in the city and the worst-kept secret on the waterfront: half the harbour's smuggling moves through the back rooms while half the council drinks out front. He has never held the gun. He holds the ledger, and the ledger holds everyone.

What he wants is respectability. It's the one thing he can't buy — and the one thing I can take from him.
The Penguin.associates: The Iceberg Lounge staff; harbour crews; councillors on retainer
The Penguin.weakness: Vanity, and the respectability he can't buy
The Penguin.contingency: Follow the money, not the man — his books put him away; his fists never will.

The Riddler.bio:
Edward Nygma would rather be caught than be thought stupid. That's the whole file, really; the rest is detail.

Every crime comes with a riddle, because getting away with it was never the point — someone has to know he was cleverer. Ciphers in the classifieds, question marks in the snow, deathtraps with a way out only he thinks is fair.

Solve it fast and he sulks. Solve it faster than he planned and he comes apart. He thinks I'm the only one in Gotham worth playing against. I wish he were wrong.
The Riddler.contingency: Solve it faster than he expects, then don't tell him how — the not-knowing breaks him.

Two-Face.bio:
Harvey Dent was my friend — the best district attorney this city ever had, and the only man who ever made me believe Gotham might be saved in daylight.

Sal Maroni threw acid in his face from the witness stand. The surgeons saved half of it. The coin took the rest. Every choice goes to the flip now; every crime comes in twos.

I still talk to Harvey when I find him. I don't talk to the coin. Some nights he answers me. Those are the nights I keep doing this for.
Two-Face.associates: Twin-themed crews; the Falcones, on and off
Two-Face.weakness: The coin — and the Harvey still in there
Two-Face.contingency: Talk to Harvey, not Two-Face. Control the coin and you control the outcome.

Scarecrow.bio:
Dr. Jonathan Crane taught psychology at Gotham University until they found out what he was doing to his students in the name of research. He's been doing it to the rest of the city ever since.

His toxin makes you live your worst fear for as long as he likes, and he takes notes while you do. I've breathed it. I know what I saw. I'll never tell anyone.

He's afraid of exactly one thing, and I make sure it's the last thing he sees. Filters in every cowl, antidote in every belt — and never fight in a dark he chose.
Scarecrow.associates: Hired thugs; occasionally the League of Shadows
Scarecrow.weakness: His own fear — of bats, of being afraid
Scarecrow.contingency: Filters in every cowl; antidote in every belt. Don't fight in the dark he's chosen.

Poison Ivy.bio:
Pamela Isley was a botanist whose mentor tried to kill her with his own toxins. The plants answered instead, and she's been answering for them ever since.

She would tear Gotham up by the roots to let the forest back in — and on her calmer days she makes an argument about what this city has done to the ground it stands on that I can't entirely refute. That's what makes her dangerous. Her pheromones work on anyone who breathes.

Harley is the only person she'd put above a tree. Some nights that's the most hopeful thing in my files.
Poison Ivy.contingency: Women and filtered air against the pheromones. Never fight her in a greenhouse.

Mr. Freeze.bio:
Victor Fries is the saddest man I've ever had to fight. His wife, Nora, has been frozen in a chamber for years, waiting for a cure he hasn't found, and everything he's ever stolen has been for her.

The cold keeps him alive; grief keeps him merciless. He doesn't want the city, or money, or me. He wants time, and there's never enough of it.

I'll threaten the suit if I have to. I will never threaten Nora. He knows that, and it's the only reason he still talks to me.
Mr. Freeze.contingency: Thermite and a heat source; threaten the suit, never Nora.

Bane.bio:
He was born in Peña Duro, serving his father's life sentence before he could walk. He read every book in that prison, taught himself to fight in the dark, and walked out the strongest man in it with Venom in his veins.

He studied me for months before he came to Gotham. He emptied Arkham to wear me down, waited until I could barely stand, and broke my back across his knee. A strategist first, a giant second.

He doesn't want Gotham. He wants to prove it never needed me. Never let him choose the ground or the hour — and cut the Venom first.
Bane.contingency: Cut the Venom lines. Never let him choose the ground or the timing.

Killer Croc.bio:
Waylon Jones was born with skin that scaled and a temper the world kept giving him reasons for. They put him in a sideshow before they put him in a cell, and he decided that if everyone was going to call him a monster, he'd stop arguing.

He lives below the docks now, in tunnels the city forgot, and eats what he catches. Not all of it is fish.

He tracks by smell and hates the cold. I don't follow him into the water. I make him come out.
Killer Croc.weakness: Cold, and smell — he tracks by scent
Killer Croc.contingency: Stay out of the water and the sewers. Sedatives sized for an elephant.

Black Mask.bio:
Roman Sionis carved his mask from his father's coffin. That's the man, in one sentence.

The False Face Society is the most organised crime this city has seen since Falcone and the cruellest it's ever seen. He runs it on torture and paranoia, and he takes disrespect personally — fatally.

The paranoia's what I use. He kills the lieutenants he suspects. I give him reasons to suspect them.
Black Mask.weakness: Rage — he can't stand being disrespected
Black Mask.contingency: Turn his lieutenants. He kills the ones he suspects, so make him suspect them.

Mad Hatter.bio:
Jervis Tetch hides mind-control circuits in hat bands and plays out Wonderland with real people. He's small, softly spoken and impeccably polite, and he's the rogue I'd least want anywhere near a child.

The girls he 'casts' as his Alice are why he never comes out of Arkham, if I have anything to say about it. I have a great deal to say about it.

Shielded cowls against his frequencies. Find the hat, find the signal — then find the girl, before anything else.
Mad Hatter.contingency: Shielded cowls against his frequencies. Find the hat, find the signal.

Victor Zsasz.bio:
No ideology. No gang. No endgame. He believes life is meaningless and that killing someone sets them free, and he carves a tally mark into his own skin for every one.

He's running out of skin.

Arkham's maximum wing holds him. I check that it still does more often than I check on anyone else in there.
Victor Zsasz.contingency: Never let him reach a crowd. Arkham's maximum wing, permanently.

Firefly.bio:
Garfield Lynns built explosions for the movies until he realised he liked the fires more than the films. Now it's a flame-retardant suit, a jetpack, and an arsonist's patience.

Half of old Gotham is timber and history, and he takes that as an invitation. He doesn't want money. He wants to watch.

Fire crews on standby the moment he's sighted. Ground him — the tanks, never the man.
Firefly.contingency: Fire crews on standby. Ground him — shoot the jetpack, not the man.

Hush.bio:
Tommy Elliot. We grew up a mile apart and played in each other's gardens. When we were boys he cut the brakes on his parents' car for their money, and my father saved his mother on the operating table. He's hated me ever since — for having what he wanted, and losing it the way he'd planned to lose his.

He became a brilliant surgeon so he could take faces off. Then he wrapped his own in bandages and came for mine.

He knows who I am. Of everything in these files, that's the line that keeps me awake.
Hush.contingency: He knows the secret. Everything he holds must be assumed compromised; keep the family's identities moving.

Clayface.bio:
Basil Karlo was a horror-film actor nobody remembered, until he made himself into something nobody could forget. He's clay now: any face, any voice, any body. Yours. Alfred's. Mine.

He still treats every crime as an audition and every face as a part. He's never once been offered the lead.

The family has challenge phrases because of him. Electricity and dry heat. And when someone I love says something they'd never say, I trust the doubt first.
Clayface.contingency: Challenge phrases with the family. Sonic and electrical disruptors.

The Ventriloquist.bio:
Arnold Wesker wouldn't hurt a fly. Scarface, the dummy on his arm, runs a crew, orders hits, and calls Wesker an idiot in front of the men.

Take the dummy and Wesker begs for his life, and means it. Leave it on his hand and somebody ends up in the river.

I've arrested them both more times than I can count, and I've never been entirely sure which one I was arresting.

Professor Pyg.bio:
Lazlo Valentin wears a pig's head, sings while he cuts, and 'perfects' people into Dollotrons — masked, lobotomised, obedient. The surgery doesn't come out.

He talks about beauty. He is the ugliest thing in these files.

Find the operating theatre fast. Every hour he's loose is another face gone.
Professor Pyg.contingency: Find the operating theatre fast — every hour is another victim.

Calendar Man.bio:
Julian Day commits his crimes on holidays and talks in dates. He's patient, precise, and a great deal smarter than the costume suggests.

From his cell at Arkham he's the consultant the GCPD hates calling and calls anyway. He's usually right. It always costs something.

I look at the calendar every morning because of him. Use him; never trust him.
Calendar Man.contingency: Watch the holidays. Use him, never trust him.

Deathstroke.bio:
Slade Wilson: an army experiment that made him faster, stronger and sharper than a man should be, and a soldier who turned it into the highest rate in the world.

He's only in Gotham when someone has paid for a death. He fights like a chess player who already knows the ending, and he usually does.

I don't fight him fair. I find the contract and make it worthless. Then he has no reason to be here — and he's nothing if not a professional.
Deathstroke.contingency: Find who hired him and void the contract. Never fight him fair.

Ra's al Ghul.bio:
The Demon's Head. Centuries old, renewed in the Lazarus Pits, master of the League of Assassins, and certain the world needs cleansing — of most of us, by him.

He calls me Detective. He wants me as his heir and Talia as my wife, and in all his long life nobody has told him no as often as I have.

The most dangerous thing about Ra's isn't the League, or the Pits. It's that he respects me — and he's patient enough to wait for me to agree.
Ra's al Ghul.weakness: The Pits — and his respect for Bruce
Ra's al Ghul.contingency: Find the nearest Lazarus Pit. Talia is the only door that opens.

Hugo Strange.bio:
A psychiatrist who has studied me for longer than anyone outside the family, and believes he understands me better than I understand myself. He doesn't want to cure Batman. He wants to be him — or own him.

He's profiled every one of us. He's probably right about some of it.

So I change the patterns he'd predict, and I never let him see what I'm thinking. He takes notes on everything else.
Hugo Strange.contingency: Assume he's profiled the whole family. Change patterns he'd predict.

Man-Bat.bio:
Dr. Kirk Langstrom wanted to cure his own deafness and reached for bat DNA. Some nights he's a husband and a scientist; some nights he's something with a nine-foot wingspan and no memory of it in the morning.

Francine keeps the serum, and the faith. I keep a sonic emitter.

He's a patient, not a target. I treat him like one, even when he's trying to take my head off.
Man-Bat.associates: His wife, Francine, who keeps the cure
Man-Bat.contingency: Sonic emitter, then the serum. He's a patient, not a target.

Carmine Falcone.bio:
The Roman. Old Gotham's mob: judges, police captains and harbour masters on his books since before I put on the cowl — some of them since before my parents died.

He was the first thing I went after when I came home, and the reason I learned that fists don't close cases. Jim Gordon and the ledgers do.

He loves his family. It's the only thing about him I've ever understood, and the only lever that's ever moved him.
Carmine Falcone.contingency: Gordon and the books. RICO, not fists.

Sal Maroni.bio:
Falcone's rival for most of my life, and the man who threw acid in Harvey Dent's face from the witness stand.

He's locked up. He still runs rackets through his lawyers, and he still sleeps badly, because Two-Face wants him dead.

Keeping Maroni alive is part of the job. I do it for Harvey's sake, not his.
Sal Maroni.contingency: Keep him away from Harvey — for Harvey's sake as much as his.

Rupert Thorne.bio:
He owns councilmen the way other men own suits — a few for every occasion, all tailored. He never raises his voice and never his hand. Debts are always collected; never by him.

His weakness is paper. Every vote he's bought leaves a trail, and I read the minutes.
Rupert Thorne.contingency: Follow the council votes. His money talks, so listen.

Killer Moth.bio:
Drury Walker wanted to be the anti-Batman: the costumed hero criminals could hire for protection. It went exactly as well as you'd think.

A moth suit, a cocoon gun, and a genuine, wounded fury that nobody takes him seriously. Nobody does.

Tim insists on handling him personally. Tim is allowed.
Killer Moth.contingency: Tim can handle it. Tim insists on handling it.

The Court of Owls.bio:
There's a nursery rhyme in Gotham about owls who watch from the dark and rule from behind the walls. I heard it as a boy and believed for years that it was only a rhyme.

They're the city's oldest families, older than its charter, watching from inside the stonework — and their Talons are killers who don't stay dead. They kept me in their labyrinth for a week to teach me who really owns Gotham. I came out. I'm still not sure I won.

Cold storage for any Talon. And I don't trust anyone whose family name is on a Gotham street sign — my own included.
The Court of Owls.associates: The Talons; old families nobody suspects
The Court of Owls.contingency: Cold storage for any Talon. Trust no one whose family name is on a Gotham street sign.
